$comment: Everyday stories, noun Capability, part 1 of 2 (capability, capabilityAuth, capabilityContractSchemaRef, capabilityOperation, capabilityOperationError, capabilityPolicy). Same style rules as stories-pilot.json. Owner reviews each part.

stories.capability.adapter: A shop's app has to send e-mail, call a payment service and store files, and each of these needs a plug that fits. Adapter names the plug a capability is bound to, such as an HTTP connector, an AI service, a file store or an SMTP mailer. Without it, the deployment's usual default is used.
stories.capability.http: A capability that talks to a shipping company's web service needs its address and the way to log in. Http holds those connection settings. It is used when the capability is an HTTP connector.
stories.capability.inbound: A payment company calls the shop's app by itself when a payment arrives. Inbound declares the door, a webhook address, through which such outside calls come in to this capability.
stories.capability.name: A flow that says 'charge the card' needs a name for the ability it calls, such as 'Payments'. Name is that handle. Capability-call steps and webhook triggers refer to it, and in a pack it becomes pack-qualified.
stories.capability.operations: A payments ability can charge, refund and check a status. Operations lists what flows may call on it. Each entry is just a name, or a full description with its input, output and rules.
stories.capability.specializes: A pack offers a standard payments ability, and a shop wants it with small changes. Specializes names that base capability, and the new one builds on it instead of copying it.
stories.capability.type: Tools and people like to know what kind of ability this is, such as a payment, a notification or an HTTP connector. Type is that free label. Tooling and specialization use it.
stories.capability.uid: A capability called 'Payments' is renamed to 'Billing'. Without a sticker on it, NPDev could think the old one vanished and a new one appeared. Uid is a stable identity number, made once and never reused, so the rename is recognised. It is optional.
stories.capabilityAuth.roles: Only the finance team should be able to issue refunds. Roles lists the role names allowed to call the operation, and a caller needs at least one of them.
stories.capabilityContractSchemaRef.conceptRef: An operation 'create invoice' takes exactly what an invoice record looks like. Concept ref names the concept whose shape is the type of the operation's input or result.
stories.capabilityContractSchemaRef.schemaRef: Several operations share the same description of a 'payment request'. Schema ref names a declared schema to use as the type, so it is written once.
stories.capabilityOperation.auth: Charging a card is more delicate than checking a status. Auth says which roles and scopes a caller must hold to call this operation.
stories.capabilityOperation.errors: The payment service can refuse a card, or be unavailable. Errors lists the failures an operation can end with, each named and classified, so a flow can react to each differently.
stories.capabilityOperation.http: The operation 'track parcel' is, in the end, one request to the carrier's website. Http describes that request: method, path, parameters and body. It is used when the capability is an HTTP connector.
stories.capabilityOperation.input: The operation 'charge' needs an amount and a card token. Input is the type of what the caller must hand over, either a reference to a declared schema or concept, or an inline description.
stories.capabilityOperation.name: A flow step has to say which operation of the capability it calls, such as 'charge'. Name is that handle, used in the capability-call step.
stories.capabilityOperation.output: The operation 'charge' answers with a receipt number and a status. Output is the type of that result, written in the same forms as the input.
stories.capabilityOperation.policy: Calling an outside service can be slow or flaky. Policy sets how this operation protects itself: retries, a timeout, a circuit breaker, a limit on parallel calls and protection against repeats.
stories.capabilityOperationError.classification: A 'card declined' will not get better by trying again, but 'service busy' might. Classification says whether the error is transient, permanent or a broken contract, so retries only happen where they make sense.
stories.capabilityOperationError.description: A person reading the model should know when 'CARD_DECLINED' happens. Description is one sentence that says when the error occurs.
stories.capabilityOperationError.name: A flow wants to react specially to 'CARD_DECLINED'. Name is the error's own name, a code callers can match.
stories.capabilityPolicy.bulkheadMaxConcurrent: The carrier's website accepts only a few requests at a time, and a busy morning could flood it. Bulkhead max concurrent is the largest number of calls in flight at once for this capability. The rest wait their turn.
stories.capabilityPolicy.circuitOpenAfterFailure: When the payment service is down, trying again and again only makes everybody wait. Circuit open after failures is the number of failures in a row after which the circuit breaker opens, and calls fail fast.
stories.capabilityPolicy.circuitOpenMs: After the breaker has opened, it should give the service some time to recover. Circuit open milliseconds is how long it stays open before one trial call is allowed.
stories.capabilityPolicy.failureClassification: Most failures of a payment call are temporary. Failure classification sets how failures of this call are classified by default, unless a specific error says otherwise.
stories.capabilityPolicy.idempotencyKeyField: A customer double-clicks 'Pay' and the card is charged twice. Idempotency key field names an input box, such as the order number, whose value recognises a repeated call, so the same request is not done twice.
stories.capabilityPolicy.retryCount: A call to the carrier fails now and then for no reason. Retry count is how many times a failed call is tried again.
stories.capabilityPolicy.retryDelayMs: Trying again at once usually fails again. Retry delay is how many milliseconds to wait between retries.
stories.capabilityPolicy.timeoutMs: A flow cannot wait for a silent service forever. Timeout is how many milliseconds a call may last before it is abandoned.
